chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, raising it, said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa (peace be upon him): 'Do not kill the Samiry, for he is generous.'

key_terms.السَّامِرِيَّ: The Samiry (a specific individual, maker of the golden calf)

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah command Prophet Musa not to kill the Samiry?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* presents a unique exegetical perspective where Allah commands Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) to spare the Samiry specifically due to his *sakha'* (generosity), a trait often overlooked in his narrative of idolatry. Shia scholars highlight this to illustrate that divine mercy can be extended based on specific virtuous attributes, even within those deserving of punishment, emphasizing the multifaceted nature of human character in Islamic theology. The chapter's focus on 'al-Jawad' (the Benevolent) underscores how generosity serves as a key criterion for divine favor and preservation of life.

en.hubeali: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto Musa<sup>as</sup>: “Do not kill Samiry<sup>la</sup> for he<sup>la</sup> is a generous one’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated in a marfu‘ manner saying: “
He (the Imam) has said, ‘Allah the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, sent revelation to Moses and told him not to kill the Samiriy because he was a generous person.”
